reports.title: One month on: 62,665 people affected; 2,731 still in 100 shelters
reports.summary: SINAPROC Comunicado #30 (to 8 Nov): 19,666 families (62,665 people) affected; 2,731 people (765 families) remain in 100 shelters; COE handled 13,259 reports of structural damage in 30 days; 6,544 hygiene kits and 6,428 mattresses delivered.

reports.title: COE: 19,865 homes evaluated, 4,633 with total damage
reports.summary: COE balance to 2 Nov: 19,865 homes evaluated: 4,633 total damage, 11,107 moderate or partial, 4,125 minor; 63,767 people inspected; 3,356 people in 113 shelters (Veraguas 1,635, Los Santos 1,153, Herrera 359).

reports.title: M5.8 and M5.9 aftershocks near Tonosí on 31 Oct; Cañas left without power
reports.summary: Two aftershocks of M5.8 and M5.9 struck near Tonosí on 31 Oct; SINAPROC reported possible additional damage to already-damaged homes, no injuries; Cañas lost power and mobile signal; MOP found no new road or bridge damage. Another M5.0 east of Tonosí followed on 6 Nov.

reports.title: IGC-UP: 1,483 aftershocks and 12,251 landslides; aftershock rate down ~80%
reports.summary: One-month update from the University of Panama Geosciences Institute: 1,483 aftershocks located; daily average fell from 102 in the first week to 21 in the last; 12,251 landslides mapped on Sentinel-2 imagery (6,086 in the epicentral zone), concentrated around Torio, La Cabuya, Los Planes and western Veraguas.

reports.title: Insurers: 6,453 claims and B/.108.7M in reserves
reports.summary: The Panamanian insurers' association (APADEA, 19 insurers) reports 6,453 earthquake damage claims and preliminary reserves of B/.108.7 million as of 31 Oct; figures will change as inspections continue.

reports.title: Government: 300+ homes under construction, 1,200 jobs, 'no fiscal ceiling' for reconstruction
reports.summary: One-month briefing: 3,500 housing solutions planned (new, rebuilt or repaired); 311 homes in demolition, debris removal or construction (Los Santos 92, Chiriquí 85, Coclé 67, Herrera 29, Veraguas 38); first rebuilt home delivered in Quebrada Grande (Soná); 1,200 jobs; the US$100M emergency allocation may be raised; deadline for replacement homes 31 March 2027.

reports.title: MEF: under US$20M disbursed so far; requests near US$80M
reports.summary: Finance Minister Felipe Chapman said disbursements from the US$100M emergency trust at Banco Nacional do not exceed about US$20M, while requests (mainly MIVIOT and MOP) approach US$80M; funds are released as works advance. Banco Nacional pays contractors per five homes built.

reports.title: Photo: Tonosí — 1,600 structures affected, ~110 homes to demolish
reports.summary: Secretary Icaza: 1,600+ structures affected in Tonosí; of ~1,000 homes evaluated, ~110 must be demolished and rebuilt and ~600 repaired. Debris removal started at Hotel El Valle and the Tonosí shopping centre; the Búcaro road has a ~2 m offset and must be redesigned; site preparation for a modular hospital.
reports.image_caption: Collapsed building being cleared in central Tonosí

reports.title: Photo: demolition of quake-damaged schools starts in Coclé
reports.summary: MEDUCA began demolishing structurally damaged schools in Coclé, starting with Escuela Bilingüe Sagrejá (Toabré), San Isidro and El Potrero (La Pintada); five Coclé schools will be demolished and rebuilt for 2027. Nationally, 1,342 of 2,000 schools inspected are operating; 27 schools in Bocas del Toro, Chiriquí and Ngäbe-Buglé reopen on 11 Nov.
reports.image_caption: Backhoe demolishing a damaged school in Coclé

reports.title: UNICEF: 90,000 students affected; 15,000 children with severe impacts
reports.summary: UNICEF: more than 90,000 students directly affected and at least 15,000 children and adolescents severely affected; 11 temporary learning spaces for ~3,000 students in Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos; water and sanitation for 343 displaced people from Isla Cañas; one hantavirus case in Los Santos.

reports.title: MICI: 73 firms report losses; 12 cut staff
reports.summary: Commerce Ministry with CONEP and Fedecámaras: 73 of 370 firms contacted (from 454 in affected areas) report structural damage, lost sales or shutdowns; 12 firms cut staff affecting 31 workers; 25 priority cases need technical or financial support; report goes to Cabinet.

reports.title: Colón: 200+ families to be relocated to Alto de los Lagos
reports.summary: More than 200 families from downtown Colón whose buildings cracked in the quake await relocation to the Alto de los Lagos housing project between November and December; vacated buildings will be demolished or closed.

reports.title: Mulino commits funds for an earthquake early-warning system; USGS to study faults
reports.summary: President Mulino said the Government will pay for an earthquake early-warning system (IGC-UP estimates US$1.5–3M) and Panama will join Android quake alerts; SINAPROC and IGC-UP budgets for 2027 raised. USGS will send about five fault specialists to study the Azuero–Soná system.

reports.title: M3.9 near Arraiján on the Pedro Miguel fault; Metro briefly evacuated
reports.summary: An M3.9 earthquake ~4 km NW of Arraiján (5 km deep) on 4 Nov was felt in Panama City; the Metro evacuated stations as a precaution. IGC-UP links it to the Pedro Miguel fault (79 events since 2019), not to the Azuero aftershocks. No damage.

reports.place: Ciudad de la Salud, Panama City
reports.title: Third death: 86-year-old woman treated since 14 Oct
reports.summary: The Social Security Fund confirmed that an 86-year-old woman who had been receiving specialised care at Ciudad de la Salud since 14 Oct died on 30 Oct, raising deaths associated with the earthquake to three.
